subject: Distribution of warm up iterations over adaptation of fast and slow parameters?

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Distribution of warm up iterations over adaptation of fast and slow parameters?
parts:
Hello,

[Background: I am trying to fit a model that is extremely slow
and I am now investigating the possibility to save time by reducing
the number of warm up iterations (which is slow due to a  
small step size). Details here: 
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!category-topic/stan-users/general/KWzdLTVLILI)



Is it correct that the distribution of 150 warm up iterations is

75 iterations fast adaption
25 iterations slow adaptation
50 iterations fast adaptation

whereas if one uses 149 warm up iterations the distribution is 

23 iterations fast adaptation
113 iterations slow adaptation
14 iterations fast adaptation
 ?

This seems to be implied by the default adaptation parameters 
and stan's behavior if one specifies fewer than 150 warm-up
iterations.

It would also seem to me that if one specifies exactly 150 warm up 
iterations, adaptation intervals for slow adaptation will not expand 
as described in the stan language reference.  (I am not sure what 
happens if one specifies e.g. 180 warm up iterations, so that the 
total number of slow warm up iterations is not a multiple of 25.)

So it appears to me that if one uses relatively few warm up iterations, 
one should better also set init_buffer, term_buffer, and window 
(and not only the total number of warm up iteration.)
Is this correct?*

Finally:
How can I determine how many warm up iterations are needed,
or if adaptation was successful?

Best - Guido

* If yes, an immediate follow up questions is if I have e.g. 75 
iterations for slow parameter adaption: Is it better to have one 
75 iteration window, or is it better to set window=25 to get one 25
 and one 50 iterations wide window?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Distribution of warm up iterations over adaptation of fast and slow parameters?
parts:
Tweaking warmup isn’t going to help.  

There are two possibilities for why your step size is small.
Either your posterior is really complex and the step size
needs to be small to report accurate results, in which case
warmup is working as it should, or your posterior has a
pathological region that causes adaptation to decrease
the step size to zero.  In the latter warmup is still doing
what it is supposed to do and tweaking it won’t make the
pathological region go away.

If you step size is small but nonzero, say around 1e-4 or 1e-5
then you just have a complex model and there’s not much
you can do besides decor relation parameters by implementing
your model in another way.

If your step size is equivalent to floating point zero, around 1e-15
or lower, then you have pathological regions and HMC isn’t
going to be able to do much of anything (nor is any other 
algorithm).  This is often due to very bad nonlinear non-identifiabilties
and in this case you’ll definitely have to tweak your model.
You can play around with centering vs noncentering various
groups as well as the carful specification of priors.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Distribution of warm up iterations over adaptation of fast and slow parameters?
parts:
Thanks Michael,
this is helpful. The step size is around 1e-05 / 1e-04, so the problem seems really to be that the model has many parameters (the model code is in the topic I linked to in my original question).

Shouldn't I be able to save some time by shortening the warm up? Given that one iteration takes more than 1h when the step size is so small during warm up, it would be nice to have as few warm up samples as possible.

in another model I observed that the step size became much (and number of leapfrogs smaller) larger later during warm up. is this a general behavior?

I can look at the evolution of the step size to see if it converged. Is there a way to assess if the mass matrix is OK?

Guido

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Distribution of warm up iterations over adaptation of fast and slow parameters?
parts:
Hello Michael,

I am attaching a figure with the evolution of step size and n leapfrog steps.
dotted vertical lines delineate warm up phases and the solid vertical lines
delineates the end of the warm up.

As you can see, up to ~65 000 leapfrogs are done per iteration during warm up,
before the the step size goes down in in the terminal buffer. Given that my machine 
needs 2100s per leapfrog step (warm up took nearly 6 days!) I really would like to
further reduce the number of warm up iterations. 

That is why i was asking for ways to assess if warm up was successful.
Intuitively I think that I should get away with a relatively short warm up, because 
even if my model is complex, I still have lots of data.

best - guido

PS: I have already optimized the model by using non-centered parameterization of
regression coefficients and for cauchy distributed variables.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Distribution of warm up iterations over adaptation of fast and slow parameters?
parts:
You can see exactly what happens in the code:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/develop/src/stan/mcmc/windowed_adaptation.hpp.

If you specify less than init_buffer + term_buffer + window iterations then
the partitions shrink to relative sizes, which should be indicated by a
corresponding output message.

You need the init_window to converge so that the mass matrix isn’t biased by
the tails of the posterior, a long enough intermediate window to get a good
estimate of the global (co)variances, and then a terminal window to let the
step size adapt to the final mass matrix. We default to a long window to get
a robust estimate of the global covariance to maximize post-warmup
performance. Any tweaking to try to get away with decent performance
with less warmup is entirely up to your judgment.
